items.note: Kutakeshvara Temple at Pathari (District Vidisha): Kadamba-type tri-ratha shikhara, constricted vestibule, single-bay porch; assigned to the 9th century, a Vidisha-district comparison for early Central Indian temple form.
Maladevi Temple at Gyaraspur (District Vidisha): partly rock-cut, partly structural, called a mature example of the Pratihara style with porch, hall, vestibule and sanctum with ambulatory.
Completes the Maladevi (Gyaraspur, Vidisha district) description: tri-ratha sanctum, pancha-ratha shikhara of nine turrets, doorways, labelled Yaksha/Yakshi images; dated late 9th century.
Summary of characteristic Pratihara features of Central Indian temples (tall pediments, garland-loop frieze, naga band on door-frame, vase-and-foliage, kirttimukhas, ribbed cushion capital).
